C_SAL_MAIN.statement: For every quartic Salem beta in (1,2), the unbiased Bernoulli convolution at 1/beta is singular (the literal sal:main conclusion).

C_SAL_TRACE.statement: All u_(m,j) are algebraic integers, are not half-integers, and have the manuscript's integer trace and reciprocal-shift identities.

C_SAL_CONSTRUCTION.statement: One infinite multiplier sequence simultaneously satisfies the index-uniform cosine floor, log K_m <= .75 L_m, L_(m+1) >= 2.1 L_m from m=3, and all small-error bounds.

C_SAL_LOSS.statement: The negative-index loss has recurrence S_(m+1) <= 2.0301 S_m + C and satisfies S_m/L_m -> 0; the total loss up to n is at most 2.01 S_m + C n delta_m^2.

C_SAL_WINDOWS.statement: There are at least exp(.7 L_m) disjoint phase windows, expectations at least exp(-L_m/20), and squared L2 window errors at most C exp(-L_m/2).

C_SAL_SEPARATION.statement: The Fourier averages concentrate under the sign law and vanish in Lebesgue mean square sufficiently rapidly to produce a full-law-mass Lebesgue-null Borel set.

C_SAL_NONSTATIONARY.statement: For every quartic Salem beta in (1,2) and every deterministic sequence p_l in [0,1], the law of the independent-sign series with P(epsilon_l=1)=p_l is singular; its null set may depend on the probability sequence.

C_SAL_CENTERED_WINDOWS.statement: For arbitrary nonstationary independent sign probabilities, deterministic compensation by the means of discarded trace errors yields independent modulus-one window variables with the same squared L2 error C_beta exp(-L_m/2).

C_SAL_KERNEL.statement: Universal exact algebraic identities and sequence inequalities for the bias-characteristic-function bound, cosine-floor loss budget, and the 2.0301-versus-2.1 normalized-loss contraction.
